deities: Lord Ganesha (two Swayambhu idols - Aamod and Pramod)

history.period: Ancient origins; renovated in 1912 (Shaka 1834) by Sadguru Govind Maharaj
history.summary: Shree Padmalaya is counted among the 'two and a half' (adeech) Ganapati peethas of India and is revered as the half (ardha) peeth. 'Padmalaya' means 'home of lotus' (padma + alaya), after the lotus pond beside the temple. The stone temple, built in Hemadpanthi style atop a hill and renovated in 1912 by Sadguru Govind Maharaj, houses two self-manifested coral Ganesh idols named Aamod (trunk curving right) and Pramod (trunk curving left) seated on a single Vyaspeeth - believed unique in the world. In front of the temple are the padukas of Shree Govind Maharaj and a huge 440-kg bell; several small shrines surround the main sanctum. Nearby Bhimkund pond carries the Mahabharata legend that Bhima struck his elbow into the ground after slaying the demon Bakasura to make a pond of water.

name: Shree Padmalaya Ganapati Temple
town_description: Padmalaya is a small pilgrimage village in Erandol taluka of Jalgaon district, about 10 km from the town of Erandol and 31.5 km from Jalgaon city. Erandol itself is an old town in North Maharashtra near the Anjani river. CSV town corrected: 'Jalgaon' is the district; the temple is in Padmalaya village, Erandol taluka.

travel.airport: Jalgaon Airport (~6 km from city centre; no scheduled services as of sources); nearest operating airport Aurangabad (~160 km)
travel.railway: Jalgaon Junction (~31.5 km); Erandol has a station on a branch line
travel.road: ~10 km from Erandol; ~28-31 km west of Jalgaon on NH-6; JMTU/ST buses and auto-rickshaws run between Jalgaon and Padmalaya

visitor_information.best_time: December to February (winter); Ganesh Chaturthi for the main festival
